name: 1964-designers-view
text:
# J. C. Shaw, "JOSS: A Designer's View of an Experimental On-Line Computing System",
# RAND P-2922, August 1964 (AFIPS Fall Joint Computer Conference, 1964).
# Figures 3a to 3i, "Samples of JOSS language and interaction": nine pages produced
# at a JOSS console, with U and J marked in the margin by the paper itself.
#
# U: typed by the user       J: typed by JOSS, column for column
# D: a line JOSS began and the user finished (Demand)
# P: the paper moved to a new page      ! a key pressed, or a setting
# ~: what this reconstruction types instead of the J: line above it
#
! joss 1964
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3a, PDF page 16, printed page -15-.
U: Type 2+2.
J:      2+2 =      4
U:
U: Set x=3.
U: Type x.
J:        x =      3
U: Type x+2, x-2, 2·x, x/2, x*2.
J:      x+2 =      5
J:      x-2 =      1
J:      2·x =      6
J:      x/2 =      1.5
J:      x*2 =      9
U:
U: Type [(|x-5|·3+4)·2-15]·3+10.
J: [(|x-5|·3+4)·2-15]·3+10 = 25
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3b, PDF page 17, printed page -16-.
U: Type sqrt(3), sqrt(4).
J:  sqrt(3) =      1.73205081
J:  sqrt(4) =      2
U:
U: Type sqrt(-1).
J: Error above:  Negative argument for sqrt.
U:
U: Set e=2.71828183.
U: Type log(1), log(2), log(e).
J:   log(1) =      0
J:   log(2) =       .69314718
~:   log(2) =       .693147181
# log 2 is .69314718056. JOSS dropped a nought at the end, so its log 2 was
# .693147180: one unit low in the ninth digit.
J:   log(e) =      1
U:
U: Type exp(0), exp(.5), exp(1).
J:   exp(0) =      1
J:  exp(.5) =      1.64872127
J:   exp(1) =      2.71828183
U:
U: Type sin(.5), cos(.5), sin(.5)*2+cos(.5)*2.
J:  sin(.5) =       .479425539
J:  cos(.5) =       .877582562
J: sin(.5)*2+cos(.5)*2 = 1
U:
U: Type arg(1,0), arg(0,1), arg(-1,0), 4·arg(3,3).
J: arg(1,0) =      0
J: arg(0,1) =      1.57079633
J: arg(-1,0) =     3.14159265
J: 4·arg(3,3) =    3.14159265
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3c, PDF page 18, printed page -17-.
U: Set y = 123.456.
U: Type y, ip(y), fp(y), dp(y), xp(y).
J:        y =    123.456
J:    ip(y) =    123
J:    fp(y) =       .456
J:    dp(y) =      1.23456
J:    xp(y) =      2
U: Type 1.23456·10*2.
J: 1.23456·10*2 = 123.456
U:
U: Type sgn(-3.5), sgn(0), sgn(3.5).
J: sgn(-3.5) =    -1
J:   sgn(0) =      0
J: sgn(3.5) =      1
U:
U: Type max(1,2,3), min(1,2,3).
J: max(1,2,3) =    3
J: min(1,2,3) =    1
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3d, PDF page 19, printed page -18-.
U: Delete all.
U:
U: 1.1 Do part 2 for b=1(1)a.
U:
U: 2.1 Set c = sqrt(a*2 + b*2).
U: 2.2 Type a, b, c in form 1.
U:
U: Form 1:
U: a = __   b = __   c = __.___
U:
U: Do part 1 for a=1(1)3.
J: a =  1   b =  1   c =  1.414
J: a =  2   b =  1   c =  2.236
J: a =  2   b =  2   c =  2.828
J: a =  3   b =  1   c =  3.162
J: a =  3   b =  2   c =  3.606
J: a =  3   b =  3   c =  4.243
U:
U: Type all steps.
J:
J: 1.1 Do part 2 for b=1(1)a.
J:
J: 2.1 Set c = sqrt(a*2 + b*2).
J: 2.2 Type a, b, c in form 1.
J:
U: Type all forms.
J:
J: Form 1:
J: a = __   b = __   c = __.___
J:
U: Type all.
J:
J: 1.1 Do part 2 for b=1(1)a.
J:
J: 2.1 Set c = sqrt(a*2 + b*2).
J: 2.2 Type a, b, c in form 1.
J:
J:
J: Form 1:
J: a = __   b = __   c = __.___
J:
J:
J:        a =      3
J:        b =      3
J:        c =      4.24264069
# The figure ends here. The blank line JOSS types after this is below its edge.
J?
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3e, PDF page 20, printed page -19-.
U: 2.15 Line if fp(c)=0.
U: 2.2 Type a, b, c in form 1 if fp(c)=0.
U: Type part 2.
J: 2.1 Set c = sqrt(a*2 + b*2).
J: 2.15 Line if fp(c)=0.
J: 2.2 Type a, b, c in form 1 if fp(c)=0.
U: Do part 1 for a=1(1)15.
J:
J: a =  4   b =  3   c =  5.000
J:
J: a =  8   b =  6   c = 10.000
J:
J: a = 12   b =  5   c = 13.000
J:
J: a = 12   b =  9   c = 15.000
J:
J: a = 15   b =  8   c = 17.000
U:
U: Delete part 2.
U: Type part 2.
J: Error above:  No such part.
U: Type all values.
J:
J:        a =     15
J:        b =     15
J:        c =     21.2132034
J:
U: Delete all.
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3f, PDF page 21, printed page -20-.
U: 3.1 Type x, sqrt(x), log(x), exp(x), __.
U: Do step 3.1 for x=1,2,3,100.
J:        x =      1
J:  sqrt(x) =      1
J:   log(x) =      0
J:   exp(x) =      2.71828183
J:
J:        x =      2
J:  sqrt(x) =      1.41421356
J:   log(x) =       .69314718
~:   log(x) =       .693147181
# log 2 is .69314718056. JOSS dropped a nought at the end, so its log 2 was
# .693147180: one unit low in the ninth digit.
J:   exp(x) =      7.3890561
J:
J:        x =      3
J:  sqrt(x) =      1.73205081
J:   log(x) =      1.09861229
J:   exp(x) =     20.0855369
J:
J:        x =    100
J:  sqrt(x) =     10
J:   log(x) =      4.60517019
J:   exp(x) =      2.68811714·10*43
# The figure ends here. The blank line JOSS types after this is below its edge.
J?
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3g, PDF page 22, printed page -21-.
U: 3.1 Type x, sqrt(x), log(x), exp(x) in form 3.
U: Form 3:
U: _.__   _.___   _.____   .........
U:
U: Do step 3.1 for x = 8.50(.01)8.54(.02)8.60, 9, 9.5.
J: 8.50   2.915   2.1401    4.915 03
J: 8.51   2.917   2.1412    4.964 03
J: 8.52   2.919   2.1424    5.014 03
J: 8.53   2.921   2.1436    5.064 03
J: 8.54   2.922   2.1448    5.115 03
J: 8.56   2.926   2.1471    5.219 03
J: 8.58   2.929   2.1494    5.324 03
J: 8.60   2.933   2.1518    5.432 03
J: 9.00   3.000   2.1972    8.103 03
J: 9.50   3.082   2.2513    1.336 04
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3h, PDF page 23, printed page -22-.
U: 4.1 Demand b(i).
U: 4.2 Set s = s+b(i).
U:
U: Set s=0.
U: Do part 4 for i=1(1)4.
D:     b(1) = 543
D:     b(2) = 237
D:     b(3) = 411
D:     b(4) = 733
U: Type s.
J:        s =   1924
U: 5.1 Set b(i) = b(i)/s.
U: Do part 5 for i=1(1)4.
U: Type b.
J:     b(1) =       .282224532
J:     b(2) =       .123180873
J:     b(3) =       .213617464
J:     b(4) =       .380977131
U: Set s=0.
U: Do step 4.2 for i=1(1)4.
U: Type s.
J:        s =      1
U: Delete all.
#
# P-2922 (Shaw, Aug 1964) Fig. 3i, PDF page 24, printed page -23-.
U: 6.1 Type form 61.
U: 6.2 Line.
U: 6.3 Do part 7 for t=0(h)4.
U:
U: 7.1 Type t, a in form 62 if fp(t/.5)=0.
U: 7.2 Do part 8 for x = t+h·(.5-k), t+h·(.5+k).
U:
U: 8.1 Set y = c·exp(-x*2/2).
U: 8.2 Set a = a+.5·h·y.
U:
U: Form 61:
U:   t      Integral
U: Form 62:
U: _.__     _.____
U:
U: Set a=0.
U: Set k=1/sqrt(12).
U: Set h=.1.
U: Set c=1/sqrt(2·3.14159265).
U:
U: Do part 6.
J:   t      Integral
J:
J:  .00      .0000
J:  .50      .1915
J: 1.00      .3413
J: 1.50      .4332
J: 2.00      .4772
J: 2.50      .4938
J: 3.00      .4987
J: 3.50      .4998
J: 4.00      .5000

name: 1965-examples
text:
# J. C. Shaw, "JOSS: Examples of the Use of an Experimental On-Line Computing
# Service", RAND P-3131, April 1965. Eight pages typed at a JOSS console on
# 28 April 1965 between 12:30 and 13:41, reproduced in two colours: the user in
# green, JOSS in black.
#
# U: typed by the user       J: typed by JOSS, column for column
# D: a line JOSS began and the user finished (Demand)
# P: the paper moved to a new page      ! a key pressed, or a setting
# ~: what this reconstruction types instead of the J: line above it
#
! joss 1965
#
# P-3131 (Shaw, Apr 1965) PDF page 3, printed page -2-.
# JOSS heads the page: 1230 4-28-65 JCS
P:
U: *  Some elements of the language:
U:
U: Type 2+2.
J:      2+2 =       4
U: Type 2+2+.
J: Eh?
U: Type x.
J: Error above:  x is undefined.
U: Set x=3.
U: Type x.
J:        x =       3
U: Type x+2, x-2, 2·x, x/2, x*2.
J:      x+2 =       5
J:      x-2 =       1
J:      2·x =       6
J:      x/2 =       1.5
J:      x*2 =       9
U: Type [(|x-5|·3+4)·2-15]·3+10.
J: [(|x-5|·3+4)·2-15]·3+10 =  25
U: Type sqrt(144), log(10), exp(1), sin(.2), cos(.2), arg(3,3), 4·arg(3,3).
J: sqrt(144) =     12
J:  log(10) =       2.30258509
J:   exp(1) =       2.71828183
J:  sin(.2) =        .198669331
J:  cos(.2) =        .980066578
J: arg(3,3) =        .785398163
J: 4·arg(3,3) =     3.14159265
U: Type sgn(-3.5), sgn(0), sgn(3.5).
J: sgn(-3.5) =     -1
J:   sgn(0) =       0
J: sgn(3.5) =       1
U: Type max(6·x, 20, x*3).
J: max(6·x, 20, x*3) =  27
U: Type min(6·x, 20, x*3).
J: min(6·x, 20, x*3) =  18
U: Set y=123.456.
U: Type y, ip(y), fp(y), dp(y), xp(y).
J:        y =     123.456
J:    ip(y) =     123
J:    fp(y) =        .456
J:    dp(y) =       1.23456
J:    xp(y) =       2
U: Type 1.23456·10*2.
J: 1.23456·10*2 =  123.456
U: Type all values.
J:
J:        x =       3
J:        y =     123.456
J:
U: Delete all values.
#
# P-3131 (Shaw, Apr 1965) PDF page 4, printed page -3-.
# JOSS heads the page: 1238 4-28-65 JCS
P:
U: *  Stored program for computing the hypotenuse:
U:
U: 1.1 Set c=sqrt(a*2+b*2).
U: 1.2 Type a,b,c in form 1.
U: Form 1:
U: a = __   b = __   c = ___.______
U: 2.1 Do part 1 for b=1(1)a.
U: 2.2 Line.
U: Type all steps.
J:
J: 1.1 Set c=sqrt(a*2+b*2).
J: 1.2 Type a,b,c in form 1.
J:
J: 2.1 Do part 1 for b=1(1)a.
J: 2.2 Line.
J:
U: Type form 1.
J: a = __   b = __   c = ___.______
# A blank line. Nothing on the page says who made it: taken as the user's.
U:
U: Do part 2 for a=1(1)4.
J: a =  1   b =  1   c =   1.414214
J:
J: a =  2   b =  1   c =   2.236068
J: a =  2   b =  2   c =   2.828427
J:
J: a =  3   b =  1   c =   3.162278
J: a =  3   b =  2   c =   3.605551
J: a =  3   b =  3   c =   4.242641
J:
J: a =  4   b =  1   c =   4.123106
J: a =  4   b =  2   c =   4.472136
J: a =  4   b =  3   c =   5.000000
J: a =  4   b =  4   c =   5.656854
J:
U: *  Modification to type only integral c's:
U:
U: Delete step 2.2.
U: 1.2 Type a,b,c in form 1 if fp(c)=0.
U: Do part 2 for a=1(1)25.
J: a =  4   b =  3   c =   5.000000
J: a =  8   b =  6   c =  10.000000
J: a = 12   b =  5   c =  13.000000
J: a = 12   b =  9   c =  15.000000
J: a = 15   b =  8   c =  17.000000
J: a = 16   b = 12   c =  20.000000
J: a = 20   b = 15   c =  25.000000
J: a = 21   b = 20   c =  29.000000
J: a = 24   b =  7   c =  25.000000
J: a = 24   b = 10   c =  26.000000
J: a = 24   b = 18   c =  30.000000
# A blank line. Nothing on the page says who made it: taken as the user's.
U:
U: Delete all.
#
# P-3131 (Shaw, Apr 1965) PDF page 5, printed page -4-.
# JOSS heads the page: 1250 4-28-65 JCS
P:
U: *  Integration of 1/x by Gauss two-point rule:
U:
U: 1.1 Type X,Y in form 1 if fp(X)=0.
U: 1.2 Do part 2 for x=X+p·h, X+q·h.
U: 2.1 Set y=1/x.
U: 2.2 Set Y=Y+.5·h·y.
U: Form 1:
U: __   _._____
# ?? user-typed form line partly overprinted by the next line in the scan; taken to be identical to the JOSS-typed copy of Form 1 further down (which is clear)
U: Set p=.5-.5/sqrt(3).
U: Set q=.5+.5/sqrt(3).
U: Set Y=0.
U: Set h=.1.
U: Do part 1 for X=1(h)10.
J:  1    .00000
J:  2    .69315
J:  3   1.09861
J:  4   1.38629
J:  5   1.60944
J:  6   1.79176
J:  7   1.94591
J:  8   2.07944
J:  9   2.19722
J: 10   2.30259
U: Type 10, log(10) in form 1.
# the "0" of log(10) is a strikeover: user typed "log(1)" , backspaced over ")" and struck "0" on top of it, then typed ")" again (see the user comment two lines below). Printed position holds both ")" and "0"; "0" is what JOSS used (output is log(10))
J: 10   2.30259
U: *  Notice above that JOSS allows backspacing and strikeovers.
U: Type all.
J:
J: 1.1 Type X,Y in form 1 if fp(X)=0.
J: 1.2 Do part 2 for x=X+p·h, X+q·h.
J:
J: 2.1 Set y=1/x.
J: 2.2 Set Y=Y+.5·h·y.
J:
J:
J: Form 1:
J: __   _._____
J:
J:
J:        h =        .1
J:        p =        .211324866
J:        q =        .788675134
J:        x =      10.0788675
J:        y =        .0992174964
J:        X =      10
J:        Y =       2.31253534
J:
U: Delete all.
# Six consoles were in use. Here there is one, so the transcript says how many.
! users 6
U: Type users.
J: 6
#
# P-3131 (Shaw, Apr 1965) PDF page 6, printed page -5-.
# JOSS heads the page: 1300 4-28-65 JCS
P:
U: *  Root finding:
U:
U: 1.1 Set w=y.
U: 1.2 Do part 2 for x=x+d.
U: 1.3 Set d=d·y/(w-y).
U: 1.4 To part 1 if |y|≥e.
# the "y" between the bars carries a strikeover (another character struck on the same position; looks like "|" over/under "y"); JOSS lists the step back as |y|≥e
U: 1.5 Type "Root".
U:
U: 2.1 Set y=exp(x)-20·log(x).
U: 2.2 Type x,y in form 1.
U:
U: Form 1:
U: x = __.______   y = __.______
U:
U: Type step 1.4.
J: 1.4 To part 1 if |y|≥e.
U: Do part 2 for x=.5(.5)3.
J: x =   .500000   y = 15.511665
J: x =  1.000000   y =  2.718282
J: x =  1.500000   y = -3.627613
J: x =  2.000000   y = -6.473888
J: x =  2.500000   y = -6.143321
J: x =  3.000000   y = -1.886709
U: Do part 2 for x=3.5, 4.
J: x =  3.500000   y =  8.060193
J: x =  4.000000   y = 26.872263
U: Do part 2 for x=1.2.
J: x =  1.200000   y =  -.326314
U: Do part 1 for d=-.05.
J: x =  1.150000   y =   .362954
J: Error at step 1.4:  e is undefined.
U: Set e=.00005.
U: Go.
J: x =  1.176329   y =  -.005521
J: x =  1.175934   y =  -.000092
J: x =  1.175928   y =   .000000
J: Root
U: Do part 2 for x=3.1.
J: x =  3.100000   y =  -.430091
U: Do part 1 for d=.1.
J: x =  3.200000   y =  1.269514
J: x =  3.125305   y =  -.023794
J: x =  3.126680   y =  -.001278
J: x =  3.126758   y =   .000001
J: Root
U: Do part 2 for x=x-.000001.
J: x =  3.126757   y =  -.000015
# ?? lower half of this line is clipped in the reproduction (overprinted/cut by the next line); digits 3.126757 and -.000015 read from the top halves, consistent with x=3.126758-.000001
U: Delete all.
#
# P-3131 (Shaw, Apr 1965) PDF page 7, printed page -6-.
# JOSS heads the page: 1307 4-28-65 JCS
P:
U: *  Matrix inversion with simple pivoting on the diagonal.
U:
U: 1.1 Set p=a(n,n).
U: 1.2 Set a(n,n)=1.
U: 1.3 Do part 2 for j=1(1)N.
U: 1.4 Do part 3 for i=1(1)N.
U:
U: 2.1 Set a(n,j)=a(n,j)/p.
U:
U: 3.1 Done if i=n.
U: 3.2 Set q=a(i,n).
U: 3.3 Set a(i,n)=0.
U: 3.4 Do part 4 for j=1(1)N.
U:
U: 4.1 Set a(i,j)=a(i,j)-a(n,j)·q.
U:
U: *  JOSS can help with the input:
U:
U: 11.1 Demand a(i,j).
U: 12.1 Do part 11 for j=1(1)N.
U:
U: *  For the output:
# "output": user typed "oup", backspaced and struck "t" over the "p" (position 3 of the word holds both "p" and "t"), then "put:"
U:
U: 21.1 Type a(i,1), a(i,2), a(i,3), a(i,4) in form 1.
U: Form 1:
U: __._____  __._____  __._____  __._____
U:
U: Do part 12 for *
U: *  An asterisk at the end can kill the line... I forgot something:
U: Set N=4.
U: Do part 12 for i=1(1)N.
D:   a(1,1) = 3.582
D:   a(1,2) = -.670
D:   a(1,3) = .873
D:   a(1,4) = 1.055
D:   a(2,1) = -.251
D:   a(2,2) = 4.569
D:   a(2,3) = .675
D:   a(2,4) = -.497
D:   a(3,1) = 1.675
D:   a(3,2) = -.764
D:   a(3,3) = 2.781
D:   a(3,4) = .778
D:   a(4,1) = .564
D:   a(4,2) = -.466
D:   a(4,3) = 1.387
D:   a(4,4) = 4.965
U: Do part 21 for i=1(1)4.
J:  3.58200   -.67000    .87300   1.05500
J:  -.25100   4.56900    .67500   -.49700
J:  1.67500   -.76400   2.78100    .77800
J:   .56400   -.46600   1.38700   4.96500
#
# P-3131 (Shaw, Apr 1965) PDF page 8, printed page -7-.
# JOSS heads the page: 1317 4-28-65 JCS
P:
U: Do part 1 for n=1(1)N.
U: Do part 21 for i=1(1)4.
J:   .32861    .02877   -.08326   -.05390
J:   .04839    .21513   -.07921    .02366
J:  -.19033    .04018    .42024   -.02139
J:   .02038    .00570   -.11537    .21573
# A blank line. Nothing on the page says who made it: taken as the user's.
U:
U: *  Invert the matrix back again:
U:
U: Do part 1 for n=1(1)N.
U: Do part 21 for i=1(1)N.
J:  3.58200   -.67000    .87300   1.05500
J:  -.25100   4.56900    .67500   -.49700
J:  1.67500   -.76400   2.78100    .77800
J:   .56400   -.46600   1.38700   4.96500
U: Delete all.
U:
U: *  From Litton Industries' "Problematical Recreations" we get:
U: *  Problem:  Find four digits A, T, O and M such that
U: *            sqrt(ATOM) = A+TO+M.
U: *  C. L. Baker's solution:
U:
U: Form 1:
